text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crude oil find near Lagos causes ripples as three traditional rulers in the state each claim that the area of the find is within their domain.
- Nigeria police plan to deploy 50,000 police officers nationwide to ensure peace during local council poll on a yet to be specified date next month, police sources say.
- Twelve carpet manufacturing firms have folded in Nigeria in the last four years, says president of the carpet manufacturers group David Amao.
- Four Nigerians were among survivors of a hijacked Ethiopian airliner crash into the Indian Ocean at the weekend.

- Employers association suggests policy measures for 1997 government fiscal budget to cut unemployment. They include stimulating demand for locally produced goods, improving public infrastructure, stopping factory closures by special task forces, abolition of multiple taxes and provision of industrial estates.

- Nigerian-American chamber of commerce plans trade tour of United States as part of coordinated effort to reverse the declining interest of U.S. investors in Nigeria, chamber's president Moses Ihonde tells a business seminar in Lagos.
- Central bank approves 47 private banks to handle accounts of ministries and government firms from next year, sources say.
- A retired army general, a former state governor and three others have been charged before failed banks tribunal with owing Oceanic Bank Nigeria Ltd 29.8 million naira.
